notes.purpose: MySQL 8.4. The textCollate override supplies this server's byte-exact NO PAD collation, utf8mb4_0900_bin. The MariaDB spelling utf8mb4_nopad_bin is not portable to MySQL. All other spellings are inherited from mysql-family.
notes.how-it-was-authored: Initially authored as an empty leaf and verified against MySQL 8.4.11. F2 expanded the live oracle to trailing spaces and found that the inherited utf8mb4_bin had PAD SPACE semantics. The current override was verified with comparisons, grouping, HAVING, text operations on projected keys and regex on MySQL 8.4.11.
notes.version: 8.4 is the minimum this document assumes and what every `since` is compared against. The regex functions the family relies on -- REGEXP_INSTR, REGEXP_REPLACE -- arrived in 8.0.4, so a 5.7 leaf would need most of the regex family refused; it is not written because nobody has probed one.
notes.sql_mode: Verified on 8.4.11 with the shipped default: ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, NO_ZERO_IN_DATE, NO_ZERO_DATE, ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO, NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION. The family's textEscape assumption is that NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES is off, which it is. ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO governs INSERT and UPDATE, not SELECT: SELECT 1/0 is still NULL here, exactly as on MariaDB, which is the divergence docs/SQL-TRANSLATION.md §11.1 records.
notes.identical-by-check: All five SQL case runners mirror MariaDB cases to MySQL, pinning the single intentional SQL spelling substitution from COLLATE utf8mb4_nopad_bin to COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_bin. The substitution is not read from the map, so a wrong map entry still fails. PHP additionally compares ops, funcs and skel entry by entry; skel.case is the declared caveat difference. The live oracle checks both leaf semantics.
notes.where-they-do-differ: DECIMAL multiplication caps scale at 30 on MySQL and 38 on MariaDB. The family scale-limit caveat and corpus witness both boundaries. Text identity is not a caveat: different NO PAD collation spellings implement the same byte semantics.
notes.where-mariadb-differs: MariaDB pads CASE NUM branch scales (CASE WHEN FALSE THEN 2.50 ELSE 3 END yields 3.00); MySQL 8.4 yields 3 as SEL does. MariaDB declares numeric-scale on skel.case; LEN(IF(FALSE, 2.50, 3)) witnesses the difference.
